title: detected an existing LaTeX distribution
description:
In reference to https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/39#issuecomment-469644041

I attempted to run `tinytex::install_tinytex()`, but receive:

```
Error: Detected an existing LaTeX distribution (e.g., pdftex is at /usr/bin/pdftex). You have to uninstall it, or use install_tinytex(force = TRUE) if you are sure TinyTeX can override it (e.g., you are a PATH expert or installed TinyTeX previously).
```

There seems to be a conflict between the LaTeX version that is installed by default (via yum builddep R texlive, recommended by RStudio here: https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/218004217-Building-R-from-source), and what is being recommended in the above-referenced issue.  Unless the official recommendation is to install texlive and then force the tinytex installation.

Please let me know if I have misunderstood something.  Thank you for your help.

title: tinytex installation pain on Mac
description:
I'm struggling to get tinytex up and running on my Mac.  I'd previously installed TeX Live 2018, but RStudio's knit button didn't work for me with that either, so I've done my best to get rid of it and start fresh with tinytex.  Neither CRAN or the GitHub version have worked for me.

My problem isn't #24 (sadly)--instead, `tinytex::install_tinytex()` warns it cannot find various ini files and tlmgr errors out (see below).  `tinytex:::is_tinytex()` nevertheless returns `TRUE`, but knitting a default test.Rmd gets me `Error: Failed to compile test.tex.`

title: Error using tinytex in portable mode, with tinytex::use_tinytex(). Can't knit to PDF.
description:
Moved from https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/4096

LaTex seems to have an issue with weird folder naming in the company I work for, which includes a '$' sign. Error in 'kpathsea'.  Is there a workaround?    I made some a nice report in HTML but now people want it in PDF. Cheers!

##System details
RStudio Edition : Desktop
RStudio Version : 1.1.456
OS Version      :  Windows 10
R Version       :  3.5.1
Steps to reproduce the problem
I used tinytex::copy_tinytex() to create a copy of tinytex, then used tinytex::use_tinytex() to set up my R Studio to create PDFs.

##Describe the problem in detail
I get this error:

tinytex::use_tinytex()
warning: kpathsea: //QSR-FP23.YWH.LOCAL/home-mqo-1$/User/My Documents: Unrecognized variable construct `$/'.
Use of uninitialized value in bitwise or (|) at S:\Applications\SUBSUR~1\Useful Software\TinyTeX\texmf-dist\scripts\texlive\tlmgr.pl line 1482.

Restart R and your editor and check if tinytex::tinytex_root() points to S:/Applications/Subsurface_Tools/Useful Software/TinyTeX

The tinytex::tinytex_root() command shows the right folder. But Rstudio doesn't create the PDF.

When I attempt to knit my R Markdown to PDF, I keep getting the same error all the time:
"No TeX installation detected (TeX is required to create PDF output). You should install a recommended TeX distribution for your platform: ........"

##Describe the behavior you expected
I expected to be able to knit my R Markdown document to PDF.

title: issues with system-wide tinytex setup & on-the-fly style file installation
description:
Hi @yihui ,

Sorry to bother you with this but I'm not sure where things are going wrong.

In the system-wide `tinytex` installation we have on the Rocker images, `tinytex::tlmgr_install()` seems to insist on creating a symlink to `/root/bin`, which I believe it should not be doing.  

I can get `tlmgr_install()` to work by giving the user permission to write to `/root/bin` (which clearly isn't the right solution), i.e. `mkdir /root/bin && chown -R root:staff /root/bin && chmod g+rwx /root/bin`.  But even when `tlmgr_install()` is happy:

```
> tinytex::tlmgr_install("bbm")
tlmgr install bbm
tlmgr: package repository http://mirrors.concertpass.com/tex-archive/systems/texlive/tlnet (not verified: gpg unavailable)
tlmgr install: package already present: bbm
tlmgr path add
```

Something is going wrong with the paths, because I still cannot knit an example doc like 

```
---
title: "Untitled"
header-includes:
   - \usepackage{bbm}
output: pdf_document
---
```

same error:

```
tlmgr search --file --global '/bbm.sty'
Trying to automatically install missing LaTeX packages...
tlmgr install bbm-macros
tlmgr: package repository http://mirrors.concertpass.com/tex-archive/systems/texlive/tlnet (not verified: gpg unavailable)
tlmgr install: package already present: bbm-macros
tlmgr path add
tlmgr search --file --global '/bbm.sty'
! LaTeX Error: File `bbm.sty' not found.

! Emergency stop.
```


I suspect these are all path issues related to the fact that tinytex is somehow assuming it should still be installed at the user level and not the system level, but we really would like it to work at the system-level so it can be shared across a multi-user environment if necessary.  You should be able to reproduce this behavior with a vanilla `rocker/verse` image:

title: Strange time-out - new Windows laptop
description:
My colleague just brought her laptop to me. Brand new, just bought it, Windows 10, installed R & RStudio, and wanted to get tinytex working because we're using it with our students. The installer seems to time out / lock immediately after the [09/10] tlperl.win32. It looks like the 9th item, tlperl, installs ok, but it never progresses to item 10/10. Eventually, it dies, fails to install, but acts like it has - the script just doesn't know what to do.

I tried downloading the script manually and running it on Powershell, and the same thing happened. 

I thought at first it might be network connectivity, but I've just completed the install on another laptop in the same room on the same WiFi, so likely not.

Have you ever seen this issue before? I couldn't find any error message or any details on why the process was stalling. Sorry for vague & non-reproducible example - I've never seen this happen before, and can't reproduce it outside of her specific laptop.

title: versioning tinytex?
description:
I noticed that `install_tinytex` functions points always to the latest master branch of GitHub. 

I think it would be preferable if the R function loaded the tools script bundled directly in the package, rather than from the most recent GitHub copy? (e.g. https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/blob/master/R/install.R#L95 why not `system.file()` instead?), and if the tools script itself could do likewise? or at least point tagged releases instead?)  Maybe that doesn't matter much. 

I realizing versioning the tinytex libraries itself is a different issue, might also be something to think about.

title: How to make RStudio use user-specified TeX engines?
description:
@yihui 

Related to [this question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52101025/specifing-a-bst-file-in-biblio-style-does-not-work-when-knitting-bookdown), I would like to ask what I should configure to use any TeX engines, rather than `pdflatex` when I knit a document in RStudio. My final goal is following: just pressing knit button creates the right PDF output, calling the TeX engines I want to use. 

My question may seem similar to [this](https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/issues/52#issue-330940404) but due to the difference in the final goals, I newly raised the issue.

# What I intend to do by customizing the TeX engines

I'm trying to use [`jecon-unicode.bst`](https://github.com/ShiroTakeda/jecon-bst/blob/master/unicode/jecon-unicode.bst) to produce my citation sections (I changed the file name as `jeconunicode.bst` in my working directory due to the error with the hyphen in the file name). Since, in my case, there is no `.csl` file which satisfies my citation style, I have to specify `.bst` file in `biblio-style` line in the YAML of `.Rmd` as shown below. 

## `test2.Rmd`

```md
---
title: "Title"
author: "Name"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%Y年 %B %d日')`"
output:
  bookdown::pdf_document2:
    latex_engine: lualatex
    keep_tex: yes
    toc: TRUE
    toc_depth: 2
    number_sections: TRUE
    fig_caption: TRUE
    dev: cairo_pdf
    extra_dependencies: subfig
    citation_package: natbib
link-citations: yes    
always_allow_html: yes
documentclass: ltjsarticle
header-includes:
   - \RequirePackage{luatexja}
   - \usepackage{graphicx}
   - \usepackage{float}
   - \DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.pdf,.PNG}
   - \usepackage{luatexja-fontspec}
   - \setmainfont{TeX Gyre Termes}
   - \setsansfont{TeX Gyre Heros}
   - \setlength\parskip{0mm}
   - \setlength\parindent{1\Cwd}
   - \usepackage[japanese]{babel}
   - \captionsjapanese
   - \newdimen\bibindent
   - \setlength\bibindent{3\Cwd}
bibliography: myref.bib
biblio-style: jeconunicode
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r include=FALSE}
#library(tinytex)
#Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PDFLATEX = "latexmk")
#options(tinytex.engine = 'lualatex')
options(tinytex.latexmk.emulation = FALSE)
options(tinytex.verbose = TRUE)

# 何とかの考察に関する歴史

@ST-jp は、「なんとかとは何とかだ！」[@ST-jp]と述べた。
しかし、@ST-en では一転して、
「Something should be more significant than something!!」[@ST-en]と
主張している。

# 参考文献 {-}
```

## `myref.bib`

Since [`jecon-unicode.bst`](https://github.com/ShiroTakeda/jecon-bst/blob/master/unicode/jecon-unicode.bst) adopt different citation styles according to the language, the user has to allow the `.bst` to recognize which article is written in Japanese. To do so, it is necessary to add `language = {ja}`.

```
@article{ST-jp,
title = {われらの発見について：変貌を遂げつつある何とかの将来に関する過去・現在・未来},
journal = {何十華論考},
volume = 42,
number = 5,
pages = {128 -- 182},
year = {2021},
author = {鈴木, 一郎 and 田中, 太郎},
language = {ja}
}

@article{ST-en,
title = {Our first investigation: this is not the first, but this should be the last},
journal = {Journal of Something},
volume = 23,
number = 5,
pages = {19 -- 176},
year = 2032,
author = {Suzuki, Ichiro and Tanaka, Taro}
}
```

## The example of the desirable output

By using [`jecon-unicode.bst`](https://github.com/ShiroTakeda/jecon-bst/blob/master/unicode/jecon-unicode.bst), I can cite the documents published in English in APA style. Simultaneously, I can also cite the documents written in Japanese following the style common with Japanese academic societies. I intend to make the citation section as shown below:

![](https://i.stack.imgur.com/a4K7T.png)

<!--
To complete producing a document solely with RStudio
-->

However, in order to use this `.bst` file, the users have to activate `(u)pbibtex` to resolve Japanese characters correctly.

# What I have done so far

My goal is, by `bookdown::pdf_document2` of RStudio insatlled in my Windows 10, knitting a document which finally requires `lualatex` + `pbibtex` engines to be processed rightly, as I mentioned before. 

So far, I have tried `options(tinytex.latexmk.emulation = FALSE)` on R console, following [the guide to avoid using tinytex's emulation](https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/issues/48#issuecomment-407015282), so that I can directly use `latexmk` command of TeX from RStudio, rather than `tinytex`'s `latexmk`'. Moreover, I wrote a `.latexmkrc` file to specify which TeX engines should be use to compile a `.tex` files and placed the file in R's home dir, TeX's home dir and my current working dir.  

```perl
#!/usr/bin/env perl

$latex = 'uplatex %O -kanji=utf8 -no-guess-input-enc -synctex=1 %S';
$pdflatex = 'lualatex %O %S';
$lualatex = 'lualatex %O -synctex=1 %S';
$bibtex = 'upbibtex %O %B';
$makeindex = 'upmendex %O -o %D %S';
$pdf_mode = 4;
$pdf_previewer = '"C:\Program Files\RStudio\bin\sumatra\SumatraPDF.exe" -reuse-instance';
```

However, pressing knit button (or `ctrl` + `shift` + `k`) and `tinytex::latexmk()` fail to produce the pdf output because RStudio always calls `pdflatex`. I also tried `tinytex::latexmk(..., engine = "lualatex")` but still RStudio seems to call `pdflatex`. In each way, I got `.tex` file and other auxiliary files. I also received the following error message.

```R
Latexmk: This is Latexmk, John Collins, 7 August 2018, version: 4.59.
 Error: Failed to compile test2.tex.
 Execution Has Been Interrupted. 
```

I've tried `tinytex::lualatex()`, too. However, it had stuck without any error messege, though it produced a `.tex` file and other auxil files.

Then, is there any way to force RStudio to use TeX engine which the user specifies in `.latexmkrc` file to create a PDF output?  

BTW, my attempts did created `test2.tex` and executing `latexmk test2` on the shell (Windows PowerShell, in my environment) produces the desirable PDF.

# Session Infos

```R
> devtools::session_info(('bookdown'))

title: Error when using tinytex::install_tinytex - missing argument in paste0
description:
Hi, 

I was trying to install `TinyTex` this morning via `tinytex::install_tinytex` and ran into a weird error. I got the same error from both the current CRAN release (0.7) and the current devel version. Here is the error:

```
> tinytex::install_tinytex()
trying URL 'http://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/tlnet/install-tl.zip'
Content length 349 bytes
downloaded 18.9 MB

trying URL 'https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/raw/master/tools/pkgs-custom.txt'
Content length 142 bytes
downloaded 275 bytes

trying URL 'https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/raw/master/tools/texlive.profile'
Content length 142 bytes
downloaded 295 bytes

Starting to install TinyTeX to C:\Users\Tyler.Bradley\AppData\Roaming/TinyTeX. It will take a few minutes.
Error in paste0("Next you may see two error dialog boxes about the missing luatex.dll, ",  : 
  argument is missing, with no default
Please restart your R session and IDE (if you are using one, such as RStudio or Emacs) and check if tinytex:::is_tinytex() is TRUE.
```

As expected, given the error message, when I restarted my R and Rstudio session `tinytex:::is_tinytex()` returned `FALSE`. I looked through the source code and it looks like the issue is [here](https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/blob/master/R/install.R#L134-L138). I am not entirely sure what is causing the issue, since I don't see any issues with the `paste0` call. However, this was the only thing stopping the installing. I ran `debug(tinytex::install_tinytex())` and ran everything but those few lines and it looks like `TinyTex` installed properly. After restarting my session, `tinytex:::is_tinytex` returned `TRUE`. 

I thought it was worthwhile to report this, as I am not sure whether other people have run into this before. 

Thanks for the great packages!

description:
E.g.

```R

Very minor but it might be worth expanding these paths before sending them to the associated `system()` calls.

title: "restart your R session" is incomplete
description:
Related to or continuing from #58:

I found the same symptoms (`tinytex:::is_tinytex()` returned `FALSE` after restarting R after successful installation), and they were due to the fact that R had not yet inherited the new `PATH`. This is not necessarily an R or RStudio thing, it's how the `PATH` envvar is updated and available to still-running sessions/shells.

- For RStudio, restarting the R session (via the menu or shortcut) was insufficient. Restarting RStudio fixed the symptomp.
- This is true for any IDE, really: I use emacs/ESS, and restarting emacs or just manually with something like `Sys.setenv(PATH=paste(Sys.getenv("PATH"), file.path(Sys.getenv("APPDATA"), "TinyTeX", "bin", "win32"), sep=.Platform$path.sep))`

I suggest changing the documentation (either in `install_tinytex` or in the readme/help-pages) to suggest restarting RStudio or other IDE. (You could always test that `Sys.setenv` step in `install_tinytex`, but I understand if you'd rather not mess with users' envvars.)

title: `r_texmf_path()` did not return correct result
description:
This seems to be similar with #22 . `r_texmf()` did not work for me even using the GitHub version. This led to the error when compiling package PDF manual which complained about missing `Rd.sty`.

```r
tinytex::r_texmf()
#> tlmgr conf auxtrees add '/usr/share/R//texmf'
#> tlmgr: already registered auxtree: /usr/share/R//texmf
#> tlmgr: action conf returned an error; continuing.
#> tlmgr: An error has occurred. See above messages. Exiting.
```

What caused this error is that [`tinytex:::r_texmf_path()`](https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/blob/446f17c1cf5fc6a33720087bacca9468f15b1642/R/tlmgr.R#L175) did not return correct path. The correct path should be `/usr/share/texmf` on my computer.

```r
tinytex:::r_texmf_path()
#> [1] "'/usr/share/R//texmf'"
```

```bash
ls -la /usr/share/R
# total 44K
# drwxr-xr-x  10 root root 4.0K 8月   1 23:21 .
# drwxr-xr-x 226 root root 4.0K 8月   8 08:58 ..

# drwxr-xr-x   3 root root 4.0K 8月   1 23:21 Rd
# drwxr-xr-x   2 root root 4.0K 8月   1 23:21 sh
```

I am using [Manjaro Linux (17.1.11)](https://manjaro.org/) and installed R using `pacman -S R`. I did not know if this is related to some specific Linux distro which did not put the `texmf` folder in the normal position.

tinytex::tlmgr_conf(c("auxtrees", "add", "/usr/share/texmf"))

I'm still struggling with fonts. How can we install ttf fonts using TinyTex?

description:
It would be nice to be able to pass a R function as compile engine. My goal is to be able to reuse some old makefiles and DOS-style bat files via system calls.

They are still more general than rubber, arara and latexmk, in particular if you need OS integration.

title: "latexmk" is missing in the windows installation
description:
It takes me a while to figure out how to build Latex file using Atom or VS Code with TinyTex. It seems that in the default installation of windows, "`latexmk`" is missing, thus causes trouble to build the tex file.

`tlmgr install latexmk` solves the problem. It will be good to install this in the default setting as it seems that both Atom and VS code latex package need it to work.

title: Problem rendering PDF on binder
description:
Hi! I have an issue rendering a PDF on binder (mybinder.org) using this repository:

I was able to get rid of some errors (like tinytex not being able to find `.sty` files) by installing the current dev version. To reproduce, you'll have to do some manual steps.

1. Launch the repo with https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/nuest/reproducible-research-and-giscience/tinytex
2. Then click on "New R Session" in the top right.

![](https://github.com/nuest/reproducible-research-and-giscience/raw/master/binder-screenshot-01.png)

3. Open file `agile-rr-paper-corpus.Rmd`
4. Click on "Knit" - Button in RStudio

The outut ends with the following error message: 

```
[...]
label: survey_results_hindering_circumstances
  |.................................................................| 100%
  ordinary text without R code

pandoc: xelatex not found. xelatex is needed for pdf output.

## Manual fix

Although the error is `pandoc: xelatex not found. xelatex is needed for pdf output.`, calling xelatex directly from the R console correctly renders the PDF based on the `.tex` file created by rmarkdown.

```
> tinytex::xelatex("agile-rr-paper-corpus.tex")
tlmgr search --file --global '/tabu.sty'
Trying to automatically install missing LaTeX packages...
tlmgr install tabu
tlmgr: package repository http://ctan.127001.ovh/systems/texlive/tlnet (not verified: gpg unavailable)
[1/1, ??:??/??:??] install: tabu [24k]
running mktexlsr ...
done running mktexlsr.
tlmgr: package log updated: /home/rstudio/.TinyTeX/texmf-var/web2c/tlmgr.log
tlmgr path add
tlmgr search --file --global '/varwidth.sty'
Trying to automatically install missing LaTeX packages...
tlmgr install varwidth
tlmgr: package repository http://ctan.127001.ovh/systems/texlive/tlnet (not verified: gpg unavailable)

[1] "agile-rr-paper-corpus.pdf"

## Further info and ideas

- The Docker image installs CRAN dependencies from MRAN set to https://mran.microsoft.com/snapshot/2018-02-28 - could that be an issue, not getting the latest packages?
- The file `install.R` is where tinytex is installed, using `reinstall(force = TRUE`. So it _should_ be available in the Docker image.
- If I comment out `latex_engine` in the Rmd's YAML header, then the error message becomes `pandoc: pdflatex not found. pdflatex is needed for pdf output.`

_Help or pointers are highly welcome!_

title: Windows install script: "Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel"
description:
## The problematic commands and error messages they generate:

```
powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/raw/master/tools/texlive.profile -OutFile texlive.profile"
Invoke-WebRequest : The request was aborted: Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel.
At line:1 char:1
+ Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/raw/master/tools/t ...
+ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : InvalidOperation: (System.Net.HttpWebRequest:HttpWebRequest) [Invoke-WebRequest], WebExc
   eption
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : WebCmdletWebResponseException,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeWebRequestCommand
```
```
powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/raw/master/tools/pkgs-custom.txt -OutFile pkgs-custom.txt"
Invoke-WebRequest : The request was aborted: Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel.
At line:1 char:1
+ Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/raw/master/tools/p ...
+ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : InvalidOperation: (System.Net.HttpWebRequest:HttpWebRequest) [Invoke-WebRequest], WebExc
   eption
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : WebCmdletWebResponseException,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeWebRequestCommand
```

## Powershell version, etc.

Running on Widows 10:

```
$PSVersionTable

Name                           Value
----                           -----
PSVersion                      5.1.16299.431
PSEdition                      Desktop
PSCompatibleVersions           {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0...}
BuildVersion                   10.0.16299.431
CLRVersion                     4.0.30319.42000
WSManStackVersion              3.0
PSRemotingProtocolVersion      2.3
SerializationVersion           1.1.0.1
```

## Other considerations

The generic fix for this issue appears to be forcing powershell to use TLS 1.2 instead of 1.0. 
As in [this StackOverflow thread](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41618766/powershell-invoke-webrequest-fails-with-ssl-tls-secure-channel).

Prefixing the Invoke-WebRequest lines with the code to change the TLS works, but it must be a temporary setting since it is not persistant across multiple calls of `powershell -Command`. I know virtually nothing about PowerShell, but maybe there is a way to set the setting globally?

I'm pretty new to Git, but have the issue fixed locally (though perhaps somewhat hackishly). I'll try to send a PR later today to fix this.

title: When installed as root, other users may not be able to use TinyTeX
description:
When installed in `/root/.TinyTeX`, other users will not be able to use the programs when the permissions for `/root` are 700. (I believe this is the default for Ubuntu.)

This can be worked around by running `chmod 755 /root` (as I've done [here](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/blob/f32b494f8/docker/Dockerfile#L48-L57)), but that's generally not desirable from a security standpoint. It would be helpful if the documentation explained another way to install TinyTeX in a way that all users can use it.

title: Feature request: Add output directory option to latexmk_emu() and global option to use a temporary directory for output
description:
Two feature requests here:

1.  Add an option to `latexmk_emu()` to specify an output directory.  This is analogous to the `-output-directory` option of `latexmk.pl`.
2. Add a global option to force `latexmk_emu()` to use a temporary directory (via `tempdir()`) for output.

I keep much of my work in a Dropbox, so it would be nice if building didn't happen in-place, as that creates a bunch of temporary files that trigger unnecessary syncing with Dropbox.  When using `latexmk.pl` I am able to specify an temporary directory as an output directory.

title: Copy (and overwrite) on successful compilation, instead of renaming existing file
description:
If the PDF output file already exists, the current behavior of `latexmk_emu()` is to rename the existing file and to move it back if the compilation failed.  

https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/blob/c7d62e178915e56728c7b591f4baa0d0f4874c26/R/latex.R#L135

This causes problems with workflows that use an external PDF viewer that monitor changes to the PDF file.  For example, [Skim](https://skim-app.sourceforge.io) on macOS will retain a pointer to the existing file (which is invariant to the renaming) and not see the newly compiled file. This also prevents the existing file from being removed.

Instead, can the behavior of `latexmk_emu()` be changed so that the output destination is given a temporary name, and then upon successful compilation the result is copied on top of the existing file?

title: tinytex fails on windows with MiKTeX installed
description:
@yihui , the CRAN version of `knitr` uses `tinytex` to render the tex file to pdf. However, `tinytex::latexmk("tmp.tex")` will always fail even for very simple tex file like below (I'm using x64 win7, with MiKTeX pre-installed): 

```tex
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
 afdasf
\end{document}
```
After some investigating, I find that :

- `latexmk` commands will always fail because it requires `Perl` to be installed. The reason I'm ok before using `tinytex` is that it's ok using `pdflatex` or `xelatex` to render the files directly.
- With `emulation = TRUE` I can see that `tinytex` will try to use `pdflatex` as well. However, the argument `stdout = FALSE` in `system2_quite()`  will always result in a fail status.   
For example, `system2("pdflatex", c("-halt-on-error", "-interaction=batchmode", "\"tmp.tex\""), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)` throws error but `system2("pdflatex", c("-halt-on-error", "-interaction=batchmode", "\"tmp.tex\""))` succeeds.   
https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/blob/09383dbefdbe760e781fd709e4c42b9cb849cece/R/latex.R#L238
- Since the default option of `tinytex.verbose` is `FALSE`, `system2_quite()` won't try the command without `stdout = FALSE` and leads to the failed rendering.
https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/blob/09383dbefdbe760e781fd709e4c42b9cb849cece/R/latex.R#L163

Yes, I can fix the issue by either : 

- install `Perl`, or
- set `tinytex.verbose` option to TRUE

However, installing `Perl` requires to download a not small package (90MB) and the administrative privilege while set `tinytex.verbose` option is tedious and always followed by an ugly warning... Anyway of quick fixing it so that I won't need to change my software or code?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8368933/37579953-1ab18dec-2b7c-11e8-9698-d0a3f32cea41.png)

Thanks.

title: tinytex(::latexmk) won't find any local *.sty files in base/main directory
description:
Hi folks,

after upgrading rmarkdown and use tinytex I found a serious bug, I think it is one.

Normally you may have a main directory in which your, lets say, test.Rmd files is. Let us guess you make a pdf (with keep_tex=true) out of it. You also uses a latex style file, name it mystyle.sty which is also in the main directory. You might render it, no problems.

BUT: If you use the latest  rmarkdown and tinytex AND use an output_directory different from the main directory, you got into trouble!

I the old day, a temporary tex and pdf file was build in the main directory and moved after that into the output_directory, everything went well. 
But now, it seems that you build the tex file first in the output_directory and rund latexmk (r something) on it in that directory, which is worse. Because the latex sty-files would not be in the search path of latex any more. 
This is extremely annoying where you use your own beamer theme files (which are .sty files). 

What might help as a quick bugfix is: Add the main directory to TEXINPUTS environment variable of the shell you use before starting any latexmk word. Something like "setenv TEXINPUTS ..:" or appropriate.

There is probably a much better solution, than my workaround... copying all tex and sty files to the output_directory is none!

Yours
Norman

title: Advice for system-wide install?
description:
Hey @yihui ,

Thanks for the ping, this looks super awesome.  Would definitely like to include this in our `rocker/verse` image (or maybe even the upstream `tidyverse` image since it's fairly small...).  

Your documentation covers a user-level install. While I think most of our rocker users work in single-user containers, it still seems we ought to install it at the system level (as we currently also do for R packages), but it would be nice to make sure the R wrappers around `tlmgr` still work, so I'm curious if you have any advice on that.  I'm thinking I would want to just set the install to maybe `/usr/local/lib/TinyTex` or something, and make that directory owned by the `staff` group (as we do for system R packages) so that any user can install the additional tex files as need.  So, is the `$HOME/.TinyTex` path hard-wired at the moment?
